quests.question: She has worked here ___ ten years.
quests.hint: 'For' is used with a period of time.
quests.explanation: 'For' describes a duration: for ten years, for a long time. 'Since' refers to the starting point.

quests.question: He has been a teacher ___ 2010.
quests.hint: 'Since' is used with the starting point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Since 2010' means from 2010 until now. Use 'since' with a point in time, 'for' with a duration.

quests.question: Please keep the door closed ___ the meeting ends.
quests.hint: 'Until' means up to and including the specified time.
quests.explanation: 'Until' means continuing to a point: keep it closed until the meeting ends.

quests.question: You must finish ___ five o'clock.
quests.hint: 'By' sets a deadline - no later than.
quests.explanation: 'By five o'clock' means no later than five. 'Until' means continuously up to that point.

quests.question: She arrived just ___ time for the opening ceremony.
quests.hint: 'In time' means with enough time to spare.
quests.explanation: 'In time' means before a deadline, with time to spare. 'On time' means exactly at the scheduled moment.

quests.question: The bus arrived exactly ___ time.
quests.hint: 'On time' means at the scheduled time, not early or late.
quests.explanation: 'On time' means punctually, at the scheduled moment. 'In time' means with time to spare before a deadline.

quests.question: She has been feeling unwell ___ last week.
quests.hint: 'Since' with the starting point (last week).
quests.explanation: 'Since last week' identifies the starting point of her illness. 'For' would need a duration: for a week.

quests.question: They didn't speak ___ three whole days.
quests.hint: 'For' with a period of time.
quests.explanation: 'For three days' describes the duration of the silence. 'During' would need a specific event: during the trip.

quests.question: She studied hard ___ the entire semester.
quests.hint: 'During' is used with a specific named period or event.
quests.explanation: 'During the entire semester' uses 'during' with a defined time period. 'For' is used with a length of time.

quests.question: He has improved a lot ___ his last evaluation.
quests.hint: 'Since' with the starting point (his last evaluation).
quests.explanation: 'Since his last evaluation' marks the starting point of his improvement.

quests.question: She will keep practising ___ she gets it right.
quests.hint: 'Until' means continuing to a stated point or condition.
quests.explanation: 'Until she gets it right' means she will continue practising up to the point of success.

quests.question: The report must be on my desk ___ tomorrow morning.
quests.hint: 'By' sets a deadline.
quests.explanation: 'By tomorrow morning' is a deadline: no later than that time.

quests.question: There was a rise ___ house prices last year.
quests.hint: 'A rise in something' is the standard noun-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'A rise in' is the standard pattern for changes in quantity or level: a rise in prices, a fall in unemployment.

quests.question: He has a great talent ___ music.
quests.hint: 'A talent for something' is the fixed noun-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Talent for' is the correct pattern: a talent for music, a talent for languages, a talent for sport.

quests.question: She has a passion ___ cooking.
quests.hint: 'A passion for something' is the standard collocation.
quests.explanation: 'Passion for' is the fixed collocation: a passion for art, a passion for travel, a passion for learning.

quests.question: He has an excellent knowledge ___ tax law.
quests.hint: 'Knowledge of something' is the standard noun-preposition pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Knowledge of' is the fixed pattern: a knowledge of the subject, knowledge of foreign languages.

quests.question: There is an urgent need ___ more nurses.
quests.hint: 'Need for something' is the standard noun-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Need for' is the correct pattern: a need for change, a need for more staff, a need for investment.

quests.question: She has a great fear ___ public speaking.
quests.hint: 'Fear of something' is the standard noun-preposition pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Fear of' is the fixed pattern: a fear of failure, a fear of the dark, a fear of flying.

quests.question: The solution ___ the problem was simple.
quests.hint: 'Solution to a problem' is the fixed noun-preposition pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Solution to' is always used with 'problem': a solution to the problem, an answer to the question.

quests.question: She wrote a letter ___ response to his email.
quests.hint: 'In response to' is a fixed prepositional phrase.
quests.explanation: 'In response to' is a fixed phrase meaning as a reply: in response to your letter, in response to the question.

quests.question: His attitude ___ work has really improved.
quests.hint: 'Attitude toward/towards something' is the correct collocation.
quests.explanation: 'Attitude toward/towards' describes how someone feels about or approaches something.

quests.question: There has been a reduction ___ staff numbers.
quests.hint: 'A reduction in' follows the pattern for changes in levels or quantities.
quests.explanation: 'Reduction in' follows the pattern: increase/decrease/reduction/rise/fall + in + the thing that changes.

quests.question: He has a strong belief ___ second chances.
quests.hint: 'Belief in something' is the standard noun-preposition pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Belief in' is the correct pattern: a belief in justice, a belief in hard work.

quests.question: They have a good relationship ___ their neighbours.
quests.hint: 'Relationship with someone' is the standard pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Relationship with' is the correct pattern: a relationship with colleagues, a relationship with customers.

quests.question: She wrote a review ___ the new restaurant.
quests.hint: 'A review of something' is the standard pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Review of' is the standard: a review of the film, a review of the book, a review of the restaurant.

quests.question: He has a real gift ___ making people feel welcome.
quests.hint: 'A gift for something' follows the same pattern as 'talent for'.
quests.explanation: 'Gift for' is the correct pattern: a gift for languages, a gift for storytelling, a gift for teaching.

quests.question: There was a debate ___ the new policy.
quests.hint: 'A debate about something' or 'debate on something' - both used.
quests.explanation: 'Debate about' or 'debate on' are both used. 'About' is more conversational; 'on' is more formal.

quests.question: He has a very good memory ___ names and faces.
quests.hint: 'Memory for something' means an ability to remember.
quests.explanation: 'Memory for' describes an ability to remember specific things: a good memory for names, dates, figures.

quests.question: She received an invitation ___ the wedding.
quests.hint: 'An invitation to an event' is the standard pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Invitation to' is the correct pattern: an invitation to a party, an invitation to the opening.

quests.question: He has a very low tolerance ___ noise.
quests.hint: 'Tolerance for something' means an ability to endure.
quests.explanation: 'Tolerance for' is the standard pattern: a tolerance for discomfort, a low tolerance for rudeness.
